meta.contrast_note: contrast_cell is PER SHAPE; null entries auto-select in the figure step by the documented rule: among non-reference cells maximize (|delta n_components|, |delta cyclomatic|, 1 - S) lexicographically
meta.mapper_cycles_caveat: Mapper graph cycles are not automatically equivalent to true topological loops in the data: the no-loop control produces short noise-scale graph cycles while its H1 diagram correctly shows no dominant class. Cycle length and scale context distinguish loop-like structure from noise.
meta.similarity_caveat: S is a custom exploratory overlap indicator (symmetric mean of best membership-Jaccard matches), not a metric and not a canonical Mapper graph similarity; it is greedy, edge-blind, and not normalized for node count, so it must not be used to rank graphs across different cover resolutions. Read it only against the pre-specified reference cell, beside component counts and representative graphs.
meta.similarity_definition: S(G1,G2) = 1/2 * [mean_{n in N1} max_{m in N2} J(n,m) + symmetric term], J = membership Jaccard. Corrected property: S=1 iff the two graphs have the same set of DISTINCT membership sets (node multiplicities and edges may differ). Not a metric; not normalized across resolutions.
meta.cyclomatic_number_definition: cyclomatic_number = E - V + C (edges - vertices + connected components): the number of independent cycles in the graph. Computed on the kmapper graph via networkx; see mapper_cycles_caveat before reading it as topology.

h1_calibration.gap_ratio_convention: r_k = p_k / p_{k+1} with persistences sorted in descending order. The rank k is known from the synthetic construction of each dataset (annulus k=1, figure-eight k=2, controls: none); r_k is NOT a universal automatic loop-counting rule, and the 'prominent' threshold (r_k >= 3) is a stated convention, not a theorem.
h1_calibration.reading: Construction implies NO dominant H1 class; gap ratios are calibration values only (R-1). Compare with the graph-cycle statistics below — this is the cycles-vs-loops contrast.
